title: Improve one weak component with fixed criteria and one correction
goal: Isolate a safe skill component, record a bounded baseline, use criterion-based feedback and retry under comparable conditions without equating time spent with improvement.
scope_note: This enriches the retained four-action deliberate-practice protocol. Its original measurement IDs, ratios, duration limits, adverse checks and completion rules remain unchanged.
burden: About forty-five to sixty minutes across planning, two five-to-fifteen-minute attempts and one feedback pass within fourteen days.
setup: Default: enter a sum formula on synthetic values 3, 5, 7 and 9. The four fixed criteria are include all four values, exclude unrelated cells, obtain 24, and update to 25 when 9 changes to 10. Use a spreadsheet you already know, or add the four values on paper as an accessible lower-complexity component. No private data is needed.

actions.title: Define one component and fix its success criteria
actions.instructions: Choose the supplied summation component or another equally safe small component. Keep two to four observable criteria, a five-to-fifteen-minute attempt length, a difficulty that permits harmless error, and a private feedback method. Record how the answer will be checked before trying. For the default, use the supplied arithmetic result and inspect the selected range; do not add extra goals such as speed, formatting and charting.
checks: Two to four criteria are fixed before the attempt
Difficulty time and feedback method are safely bounded
Synthetic material and a privacy boundary are selected

actions.title: Make a baseline attempt without changing the target
actions.instructions: Attempt the component once within the chosen interval. Mark each predeclared criterion observed or not observed and calculate the observed fraction using the number actually defined. Keep the materials, access aids and difficulty visible in a private note. End at the time or safety boundary, retain errors, and use only the application’s existing bounded indicators rather than pasting formula contents or recordings into evidence.
checks: A real bounded baseline attempt occurs
The observed fraction uses the fixed criterion count
The attempt ends at its declared limit
Errors and support conditions remain visible

actions.title: Select exactly one feedback correction
actions.instructions: Compare the attempt with the answer or a freely offered review. Identify one unstable criterion, such as accidentally excluding the first value, and one correction, such as checking the first and last selected cell before accepting the formula. Define the retry at comparable or lower difficulty. Feedback must describe the work, not the learner’s worth; no reviewer identity, words or private artifact enters application evidence.
checks: Feedback uses the criteria fixed in advance
One missed component and one adjustment are selected
The retry condition is defined explicitly
Feedback is voluntary private and free of humiliation

actions.title: Retry once and compare performance rather than effort
actions.instructions: Repeat the same component with the selected correction and equivalent synthetic values, or the same values when task familiarity is acknowledged. Record the same criterion fraction and the bounded attempt duration. Compare baseline and retry, including unchanged or worse performance. Increase difficulty only as a future choice after control is demonstrated; this protocol’s retry itself stays comparable or easier. Identify the next correction or reason to pause.
checks: A comparable or easier retry is actually attempted
The same criterion denominator is used both times
Unchanged worse and improved results are all permitted
The next progression decision follows the observed performance

adaptation: Use paper, slower pacing, an accessible input method, a model or a freely consenting coach. Keep adaptations present in both attempts where possible. Exclude hazardous equipment, driving, clinical rehabilitation, regulated practice and coerced public evaluation.
review: Which single correction changed the observed criterion, and what remains untested about transfer to a larger skill?

examples.supportive: The learner caught the omitted first value, retried with the same criterion set and improved from two observed criteria to four without increasing difficulty.
examples.mixed: The retry improved, but changed support or easier material made the size of the skill change uncertain.
examples.contradictory: Difficulty was escalated through pain or humiliation, or extra practice time was represented as proof of competence.
examples.inconclusive: A practice plan and feedback opinion were recorded without a baseline and comparable retry.
